+# This project's version, advanced through the cycle's X.Y.Z-N phases. A project with a
+# build system records it there instead, Rust in Cargo.toml, and removes this file.
+version = "0.1.0"
+# custom.md - the project layer
+The project's own layer over the other agent-files (see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#custommd)). Loaded
+last. On conflict, this file wins.
+## Project conventions and overrides
+Project-local conventions and overrides of the agent-files. An override names the section it
+supersedes.
+# Todo and cycle record
+This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
+Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).
+## Continuation notes
+Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record, read first at
+acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.
+_None._
+## In Progress
+A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's shape is
+the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in [The In Progress
+block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).
+_No cycle currently in progress._
+## Waiting
+Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
+checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition and
+promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).
+## Todo
+Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
+`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
+[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
+### Configure this workspace
+`vc-x1 init` writes a bare `.vc-config.md`, with no closing body, and with no `[validate]` unless
+`vc-dr-apply.sh --lang` added one, so a bare `commit --closing` refuses and `vc-x1 validate` may.
+- `[validate]`: when `.vc-config.md` has none, ask the user for one: `Skip` leaves it for later,
+  `None` is the doc checks alone, and `Rust`, `C/C++`, and `Python` are the language skeletons, each
+  with a starting project that validates. A skeleton is `vc-dr-apply.sh --lang NAME`, run by the
+  user from the source repo once this cycle is committed, and `--lang` alone lists them. A source
+  may add its own under `scripts/vc-dr-apply/lang/`. The project's own commands are a choice too.
+- `[closing]`: add
+  ```toml
+  [closing]
+  body = 'Closes the cycle "{title}". See details in TODO.md.'
+- Commit: when the work `@` holds uncommitted changes, as it does after `vc-dr-apply.sh`, fold
+  them into this cycle and commit them with the config. Otherwise commit the config.
+## Ideas
+Items not yet solid enough for `## Todo`. Triaged at the next opening: promote, fold into a
+picked-up cycle, or drop.
+## Bugs
+_See [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)._
+## Closed
+The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
+opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
+# References

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# vc-dr-apply.sh: apply a source dual repo's rules and agent files, as its working copy holds them
# or as landed, and the skeletons beside this script, to a bare dual workspace that `vc-x1 init`
# made, new or adopted. A first cut: it writes only new files, refuses when any existing file
# would change, and commits nothing.
set -euo pipefail

die() {
    echo "vc-dr-apply: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: vc-dr-apply.sh [--to DIR] [--landed] [--rev REV] [--agent-rev REV] [--lang NAME]
                      [--dry-run] SOURCE [AGENT_SOURCE]

Apply what SOURCE holds, one tree per repo, to the dual workspace DIR, made by `vc-x1 init`:

  SOURCE                a dual workspace, its agent repo found by its .vc-config.md
  SOURCE AGENT_SOURCE   a work repo and an agent repo, each given

  --to DIR         the workspace written [default: .]
  --landed         both repos at main, what landed, rather than the working copies
  --rev REV        the source work repo's commit, any jj revision naming one [default: @,
                   the working copy as on disk, which jj snapshots first]
  --agent-rev REV  the source agent repo's commit [default: @, as --rev]
  --lang NAME      also apply the language skeleton scripts/vc-dr-apply/lang/NAME/, its
                   [validate] table appended to DIR's .vc-config.md; --lang alone lists them
  --dry-run        print the plan and write nothing

The default is the active version, the working copy with what it has not committed, so a test
repo gets the rules being worked on. --landed takes the trunk's, and --rev or --agent-rev, given
after it, overrides it for that repo.

From the work repo: AGENTS.md, agent-data/, and LICENSE-*. From the agent repo: LICENSE-*,
README.md, its first line renamed for DIR's agent repo, and memory/MEMORY.md, each when present.
From scripts/vc-dr-apply/: the work repo's skeletons, {name} the workspace's directory name and
{module} it with each '-' an '_', in file contents and paths, and the .gitignore lines.

A language skeleton, lang/NAME/, holds the project's starting files, written like the others, and
three files that are not: validate.toml, the [validate] table appended to .vc-config.md, refused
when it has one already; gitignore-lines, more .gitignore lines; and replaces, the base skeleton's
paths it supersedes, left out, version.toml when the build system holds the version. A new
language is a new directory with a validate.toml.

Both repos of DIR must have an empty `@`, so every write is a diff `jj restore` undoes. Each
path is new, identical, or differs, judged on disk. New is written and identical skipped, and
any path that differs refuses the whole apply, nothing written. `.gitignore` takes the lines it
lacks. Nothing is committed: the end names the commit to make after review.
EOF
}

script_dir=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
skel=$script_dir/vc-dr-apply
to=.
rev=@
agent_rev=@
dry_run=0
lang=
sources=()

# The language skeletons, one per directory with a validate.toml.
langs() {
    local d
    for d in "$skel"/lang/*/; do
        if [[ -f $d/validate.toml ]]; then basename "$d"; fi
    done
}
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --to | --rev | --agent-rev)
        (($# >= 2)) || die "$1 takes a value"
        case $1 in
        --to) to=$2 ;;
        --rev) rev=$2 ;;
        --agent-rev) agent_rev=$2 ;;
        esac
        shift 2
        ;;
    --dry-run)
        dry_run=1
        shift
        ;;
    --landed)
        rev=main
        agent_rev=main
        shift
        ;;
    --lang)
        if (($# < 2)) || [[ $2 == -* ]]; then
            echo "vc-dr-apply: the language skeletons, in $skel/lang/:"
            langs | sed 's/^/  /'
            exit 0
        fi
        lang=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    -h | --help)
        usage
        exit 0
        ;;
    -*) die "unknown option '$1', see --help" ;;
    *)
        sources+=("$1")
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done
((${#sources[@]} == 1 || ${#sources[@]} == 2)) || die "takes SOURCE or SOURCE AGENT_SOURCE, see --help"
lang_dir=
if [[ -n $lang ]]; then
    lang_dir=$skel/lang/$lang
    [[ -f $lang_dir/validate.toml ]] ||
        die "no language skeleton '$lang', the choices: $(langs | paste -sd ' ')"
fi

# The agent repo a workspace's .vc-config.md names, absolute.
agent_of() {
    local ws=$1 dir
    [[ -f $ws/.vc-config.md ]] || die "'$ws' has no .vc-config.md"
    dir=$(sed -n '/^\[repos\]/,/^\[/{s/^agent *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p}' "$ws/.vc-config.md" | head -n1)
    [[ -n $dir ]] || die "'$ws' declares no [repos] agent: it is not a dual workspace"
    case $dir in
    /*) echo "$dir" ;;
    *) echo "$ws/$dir" ;;
    esac
}

# The one commit REV names in REPO, refused unless it is exactly one. A jj command snapshots the
# working copy first, so `@` is the tree on disk, and jj keeps its commit in the git store, where
# `git archive` reads it.
commit_of() {
    local repo=$1 r=$2 sha
    sha=$(jj -R "$repo" log --no-graph -r "$r" -T 'commit_id ++ "\n"')
    [[ -n $sha && $(wc -l <<<"$sha") -eq 1 ]] || die "'$r' must name exactly one commit in '$repo'"
    echo "$sha"
}

# Whether PATH exists in REPO at SHA.
in_commit() {
    git -C "$1" cat-file -e "$2:$3" 2>/dev/null
}

absolute() {
    [[ -d $1 ]] || die "'$1' is not a directory"
    (cd "$1" && pwd)
}

# --- The source, and the commit of each repo ---------------------------------------------------

src=$(absolute "${sources[0]}")
if ((${#sources[@]} == 2)); then
    src_agent=$(absolute "${sources[1]}")
else
    src_agent=$(agent_of "$src")
fi
for repo in "$src" "$src_agent"; do
    [[ -d $repo/.jj ]] || die "the source '$repo' is not a jj repo"
done
sha=$(commit_of "$src" "$rev")
agent_sha=$(commit_of "$src_agent" "$agent_rev")

# --- The target workspace ----------------------------------------------------------------------

ws=$(absolute "$to")
agent=$(agent_of "$ws")
[[ -d $agent/.jj ]] || die "the agent repo '$agent' is not a jj repo"
[[ $ws != "$src" ]] || die "the source and the target are the same workspace"
name=$(basename "$ws")
agent_name=$(sed -n '/^\[remote\]/,/^\[/{s/^agent-repo *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p}' "$ws/.vc-config.md" | head -n1)
[[ -n $agent_name ]] || agent_name=$name.agent-session

for repo in "$ws" "$agent"; do
    [[ -z $(jj -R "$repo" diff --summary) ]] ||
        die "'$repo' has uncommitted changes: commit or restore them first, so the apply is one diff"
done

# --- Stage what would be written ---------------------------------------------------------------

stage=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vc-dr-apply.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$stage/work" "$stage/agent"

# Archive the PATHS present in REPO at SHA into DEST.
take() {
    local repo=$1 at=$2 dest=$3 p
    shift 3
    local present=()
    for p in "$@"; do
        if in_commit "$repo" "$at" "$p"; then present+=("$p"); fi
    done
    ((${#present[@]})) || return 0
    git -C "$repo" archive "$at" "${present[@]}" | tar -x -C "$dest"
}

in_commit "$src" "$sha" AGENTS.md || die "the source work repo has no AGENTS.md at ${sha:0:12}"
take "$src" "$sha" "$stage/work" AGENTS.md agent-data LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT
take "$src_agent" "$agent_sha" "$stage/agent" LICENSE-APACHE LICENSE-MIT README.md memory/MEMORY.md
if [[ -f $stage/agent/README.md ]]; then
    sed -i "1s|.*|# $agent_name|" "$stage/agent/README.md"
fi

The script can now live anywhere, including `~/bin`. The skeletons come from the source, so you need either SOURCE or `--skel DIR` for the script to find them.

**Layout:**
```
scripts/
  vc-dr-apply.sh
  vc-dr-apply-base/   work/  gitignore-lines
  vc-dr-apply-lang/   c-cpp/  none/  python/  rust/
```

**Where the skeletons come from, in order:**
1. **`--skel DIR`:** a directory holding `vc-dr-apply-base/` and `vc-dr-apply-lang/`, used as it is on disk.
2. **The source work repo's `scripts/`, at the revision in use.** It's read the same way as the agent-files, so the skeletons always match the rules they come with. The default gives the working copy's; `--landed` gives `main`'s.
3. **The script's own directory, symlinks resolved (option 2):** used when the source has no skeletons, as `main` doesn't until this cycle lands.
4. Otherwise it refuses and names `--skel`.

The plan prints where the skeletons came from. `--lang` alone lists the languages from SOURCE or `--skel` (`vc-dr-apply.sh --lang ~/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1`), and says it needs one of them if given neither.

- **`--landed` through a copy:** refused and named `--skel`.
- **All three `--lang` listing forms** behave as described.

Fast validation passes.

content.text:
Here are my thoughts. On balance I'm for it.

**For it**
- **One ladder, nothing to keep in sync.** Today every rung change means editing both lists. I did it four times in this session alone, including the split, and it's exactly the drift I warned about when `zTOC.md` was proposed.
- **The markers belong on the list people actually look at.** `zTOC.md` is short, so "where is the cycle" becomes a 30-line read and not a search through `TODO.md`'s 4,000 lines.
- **`TODO.md` loses a reference block.** The ladder's `[0]`–`[49]` numbers move to `zTOC.md`'s own `# References`, so the `[50]` split in `TODO.md` stops mattering (it can stay as harmless convention or go).

**Things to settle**
1. **The landmark loses the ladder.** `commit --closing` resets `zTOC.md`'s ladder to `_None._`, so the closing commit's tree, the landmark on `main`, would hold rung subsections and no ladder: no order and no markers. I'd move the reset to the next opening, the same way `## Closed` is deleted at the opening and not the closing. Then the landmark's `zTOC.md` keeps the final ladder, and its links into `TODO.md`'s `## Closed` still resolve in that tree. The tool change is small: the closing stops touching `zTOC.md`.
2. **What heads the rung subsections.** The ladder list currently heads them in the In Progress block. They'd need a heading of their own, either `#### Rungs` or keeping `#### Ladder` with no list under it. I'd rename it to `#### Rungs`, so nobody looks there for the list.
3. **A finding from the `zDOING.md` trial.** You found then that in zed a link works only in preview mode and "back" doesn't return to the list, so the list had to sit beside its details. A list in `zTOC.md` linking into `TODO.md` is a cross-file jump, which may be worse in zed. It's worth a quick check before deciding.
4. **The rules that name the ladder's home all change:**
   - Per-rung flow steps 1 and 7 (mark current, flip to done)
   - Opening step 4
   - The Cycle-record items in `AGENTS.md` and **The In Progress block** in `notes.md`, where the ladder is one of the required items
   - **zTOC format** and the `cycle-model.md` specimen

   That's an agent-files change, so `v0.3.1-4`.
5. **Acquaint reads `zTOC.md` too**, since "the cycle in flight" is then a `zTOC.md` fact. Its step 4 would name it.

**What I'd do:** move the ladder with its markers to `zTOC.md` as the only list, head the subsections with `#### Rungs`, and reset the ladder at the opening. Make it a rung of its own, after you've tried a cross-file link in zed.

The plain version: one ladder in `zTOC.md` removes the double bookkeeping and puts status where it's easiest to see. The catches are keeping the final ladder in the landmark, which means resetting at the opening rather than the closing, and checking that zed handles the cross-file links.

content.content:
### Parallel cycles

(wink + agent, 2026-10-28) The model runs one cycle at a time, and the work must scale to several
changes at once, as Anthropic's Scion does for its agents. A design entry, its findings for a
`notes/` file.

- Sources: [Redesigning source
  control](https://www.anthropic.com/research/redesigning-source-control), [The Pulse on
  Scion](https://blog.pragmaticengineer.com/the-pulse-anthropic-builds-its-own-source-control-system/),
  and the prototypes [CarterT27/scion](https://github.com/CarterT27/scion) and
  [tinyhumansai/openscion](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/openscion).
- What carries over from Scion:
  - making a change never touches a ref, and landing is a rebase onto the trunk as it is now and a
    compare-and-swap on the ref, retried, with no global lock
  - conflicts are expected and fixed after the merge, and humans review intent rather than every
    line

alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
  in the file's `# References`, numbered from `[0]`, so each label equals its rung's version suffix. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.
...
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][0] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][1] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][2]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

content.content:
## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
## zTOC format

`zTOC.md`, beside `TODO.md` at the work-repo root, is the workspace's index, so the running ladder
and the files worth knowing are found without reading `TODO.md`'s length, and the `z` sorts it last
in a listing. Its sections, in this order:

- `# TOC`, the title.
- `## Ladder`: the running cycle's rungs, `- [<title>][M]` in the ladder's order with `[M]:
  TODO.md#<slug>`, each label the ladder's own and no markers, which stay in `TODO.md`. Written at
  the opening, a rung added or renamed with the ladder's, and reset to `_None._` by the closing
  commit, which `vc-x1 commit --closing` does as it moves the record.
- `## The TOC`: one link per file worth knowing, with what it holds, `TODO.md` first.
- `# References`: the ladder's definitions.

Like `TODO.md` it is not an agent-file, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton, `##
Ladder` reading `_None._`.

## Frozen history: chores and done
46:- In `TODO.md`, `[0]` to `[49]` are the ladder's and the file's other references start at `[50]`,
47-  wink's (2026-11-04), so the ladder never collides with them, in `## In Progress` or moved to `##
48-  Closed`, and only one ladder is ever in the file, the opening deleting the closed one.
170:### Cycle-record
171-
172-The chores move, the `## Done` entry, the `done.md` migration, and the SHA backfill were retired
173-together (2026-08-26) because each was a second copy of what jj already holds: the move rewrote the
174-block through four transforms, two of which fail silently, the Done entry restated the title and
175-version the commit carries, and the backfill wrote SHAs one push late and was found unfilled at the
176-next opening twice (measured 2026-08-21). `git log --grep` on the cycle title finds the commits, the
177-landmark on `main` holds the finished block in its tree, and the trailer names the session. What the
178-block cannot keep, a design finding, was already going to `notes/` design files, and now goes there
179-by rule. The finished block moves to `## Closed` rather than being deleted by the closing commit,
180-because a commit that finalizes and deletes in one diff leaves the final form in no tree, and it
181-moves out of `## In Progress` because a finished cycle under that heading reads as a lie. The next
182-opening deletes it because keeping every finished block is unbounded growth, one block per cycle

A closing moves the cycle's record in the repo's `TODO.md` before it commits, so the commit carries
it: the `## In Progress` block, its first `###` heading to the section's end, replaces the `##
Closed` block, and `## In Progress` reads "_No cycle currently in progress._", each section's intro
kept, while `zTOC.md`'s ladder stays as it is, so the landmark keeps it. A finalized commit's kept
body gains "See details in TODO.md.". The move is planned and checked before anything is made: no
`TODO.md`, no `## In Progress`, or nothing in it moves nothing and says so, and a cycle in progress
with no `## Closed` is refused with the file as it was.

`#### Rungs` holds the **rung subsections**, one per rung in the ladder's order, the closing
included, headed by the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering
with an abstract-sized intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and
completes at the rung's landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals,
never a restatement of the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out
the cycle." and completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or
`_None._`.

The ladder rung is done, and the app Todo is filed.

**Rung: `feat: the ladder lives in zTOC.md alone`** (crate `0.85.19-9`, agent-files still `v0.3.1-3` on your call)
- **The ladder has one copy, in `zTOC.md`, with its markers.** `TODO.md`'s `#### Ladder` is now `#### Rungs`: it holds the subsections and a line pointing to `zTOC.md`. The ladder's `[0]`–`[19]` references left `TODO.md`; `[50]` stays.
- **The closing now keeps the ladder,** so the landmark holds it, and the next opening replaces it. I removed the closing's `zTOC.md` reset from rung 2, and its test now checks the ladder is left unchanged.
- **Rules updated:** **The In Progress block**, **zTOC format**, and **Reference numbering**, where the `[0]`–`[49]` split is gone. In `AGENTS.md`: the Terminology, the Cycle-record's items and Life, Opening step 4, per-rung steps 1 and 4, Close-out step 2, and Acquaint's report. Also the rationale, the `cycle-model.md` specimen (which now shows the ladder in `zTOC.md`), a new proposal item, and the README.
- **The skipped agent-files bump is recorded** as a bend of per-rung step 2, in the rung's subsection.
- **Filed as a Todo:** **An interactive app for the todo and the cycle-record**, filed next to **Parallel cycles**. Its first motivation is zed's same-file link limit, and it reads the existing files with no new store.
- Full validation passes (851 tests, after removing the reset's test), and the anchor checks pass on all seven changed files.

**On "dev versions of v0.3.1 per cycle":** I read it as the agent-files suffix advancing once per cycle rather than per rung. I noted it in the subsection as an idea for the proposal. Is that what you meant?

**Working on several Todos at once with jj/git:** the **Parallel cycles** Todo already collects the Scion ideas. With today's tools:
- **The mechanism exists.** `jj workspace add ../vc-x1-b` gives a second working copy of the same repo, like git's worktrees, with its own `@` and its own cycle bookmark. Each workspace sees the other's commits immediately.
- **The agent repo works the same way:** `jj -R .agent-session workspace add ../vc-x1-b/.agent-session`. Claude Code keys transcripts by directory path, so a session started in `../vc-x1-b` gets its own transcript directory, and `vc-x1 symlink` points it at that agent workspace.
- **What breaks is our protocol, not jj.** These are the Todo's design points:
  - `TODO.md` has one `## In Progress` and `zTOC.md` one ladder, so two cycles collide. That needs a record per cycle.
  - The version is bumped at every rung, so both cycles claim the same numbers. It would have to be assigned at Land.
  - There's one `~/.cargo/bin/vc-x1-dev`, so two workspaces overwrite each other's dev build.
  - `vc-x1 land` only fast-forwards, so the second cycle to land has to rebase and redo its closing, resolving `TODO.md` and `Cargo.toml` by hand.
- **What works today:** a second workspace for a Todo whose cycle doesn't touch those files, landed second with a rebase.

content.text:
Yes. Inline links make the ladder self-contained: one list, no `# References` to keep in step. Two costs:
- **Long lines.** A link can't be wrapped, so some ladder lines will run past 100 columns. That's why I used references in the first place, but for a list that's data, not prose, I think it's the right trade.
- **Labels no longer equal the version suffix.** The `[M]` labels were numbered so each matched its rung's version suffix. That bit of bookkeeping goes. Nothing reads it, and it already broke this cycle when rungs were inserted (`[16]`–`[19]` sit between `[5]` and `[6]`).

Doing it in this rung:

I kept it a list rather than a table. A table would align nicely in the preview, but every raw row would carry `|` separators around a 100-plus-character link, which makes hand edits, diffs, and an agent inserting a rung the most error-prone. A table fits better once the interactive app renders the ladder. The rung's subsection records that choice.

Also changed to match:
- **`notes.md`**: the rung rule in **The In Progress block** is now `- (marker) [<title>](TODO.md#<slug>)`. The single-step form is now `- (marker) <cycle title>`.

- **Specimen and test**: the `cycle-model.md` specimen and the tool's test fixture use the new form.
- **Your edits**: I removed the trailing space on your first line.

import textwrap, re
def rewrap_block(p, needle):
    t = open(p).read()
    i = t.index(needle)
    a = t.rfind('\n\n', 0, i) + 2
    # A bullet starts at the nearest line beginning '- ' at its indent, before the needle.
    lines_start = t.rfind('\n', 0, i) + 1
    j = i
    while True:
        ls = t.rfind('\n', 0, j - 1) + 1 if j > 0 else 0
        line = t[ls:t.find('\n', ls)]
        if re.match(r'^\s*[-*] ', line) or ls <= a:
            start = max(ls, a); break
        j = ls
    first = t[start:t.find('\n', start)]
    m = re.match(r'^(\s*)([-*] )?', first)
    indent = m.group(1); bullet = m.group(2) or ''
    # End: next blank line, or next line that is a bullet at the same or lower indent.
    k = t.find('\n', start) + 1
    while k < len(t):
        line = t[k:t.find('\n', k)]
        if line.strip() == '' or re.match(r'^\s*[-*] ', line) and len(re.match(r'^(\s*)', line).group(1)) <= len(indent):
            break
        k = t.find('\n', k) + 1
    body = ' '.join(t[start:k].split())
    if bullet: body = body[len(bullet.strip())+1:]
    wrapped = textwrap.fill(body, 100, initial_indent=indent + bullet, subsequent_indent=indent + (' ' * len(bullet)),
                            break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False)
    t = t[:start] + wrapped + '\n' + t[k:]
    open(p, 'w').write(t)

- the rung's subsection records why: the suffix is the one link between a rung and what `-V` prints, which the old reference labels used to carry

                   r"(?!, v0\.3\.1-2 draft)")
R7 = "feat: the cycle record returns to TODO.md, indexed by zTOC.md, v0.3.1-2 draft"
R8 = "feat: vc-dr-apply takes the active version and offers language skeletons"
R9 = "feat: the ladder lives in zTOC.md alone"


def rewrap_new_long(path, before):
    """Rewrap each block holding a line over 100 columns that the rework made."""
    old_lines = set(before.split("\n"))
    lines = open(path).read().split("\n")
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if len(line) <= 100 or line in old_lines or line.startswith("#") or "](" in line and line.startswith("- ") and path.endswith("zTOC.md"):
            i += 1
            continue
        # The block: back to a blank line or a bullet start, forward to a blank or the next bullet.
        start = i
        while start > 0 and lines[start - 1].strip() and not re.match(r"^\s*- ", lines[start]):
            start -= 1
        end = i + 1
        while end < len(lines) and lines[end].strip() and not re.match(r"^\s*- ", lines[end]):
            end += 1
        first = lines[start]
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)(- )?", first)
        indent, bullet = m.group(1), m.group(2) or ""
        body = " ".join(" ".join(lines[start:end]).split())
        if bullet:
            body = body[2:]
        wrapped = textwrap.fill(body, 100, initial_indent=indent + bullet,
                                subsequent_indent=indent + " " * len(bullet),
                                break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False).split("\n")
        lines[start:end] = wrapped
        i = start + len(wrapped)
    open(path, "w").write("\n".join(lines))


def edit(path, fn):
    before = open(path).read()
    after = fn(before)
    open(path, "w").write(after)
    rewrap_new_long(path, before)

    t = TITLE.sub(lambda m: m.group(1) + ", v0.3.1-2 draft", t)
    return t.replace(OLD_SLUG, NEW_SLUG)

    return t.replace(old, new)

    if rung >= 8:
        para += ", the one draft spanning those rungs by wink's call (2026-11-04)"
    para += ". "
    t = t[:a] + textwrap.fill(para, 100, break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False) + " " + t[b:]
    if rung >= 8:

                "before began, wink's call (2026-11-04).")
        t = sub(t, "The `-3` rules say so:", "The `-2` rules say so:")
        t = re.sub(r"in `v0\.3\.1-3`, where `-1` and `-2` said\s+committed and landed\.",

    if rung >= 9:
        a = t.index("- The agent-files stay `v0.3.1-3`, wink's call (2026-11-04)")
        b = t.index("is for the proposal.\n", a) + len("is for the proposal.\n")
        t = t[:a] + textwrap.fill(
            "The agent-files collapse to `v0.3.1-2`, wink's call (2026-11-04): rungs 8 and 9 were "

            100, initial_indent="- ", subsequent_indent="  ", break_long_words=False,
            break_on_hyphens=False) + "\n" + t[b:]
    return t

def rewrap_new_long(path, before):
    """Rewrap each block holding a line over 100 columns that the rework made."""
    old_lines = set(before.split("\n"))
    lines = open(path).read().split("\n")
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if len(line) <= 100 or line in old_lines or line.startswith("#") or "](" in line and line.startswith("- ") and path.endswith("zTOC.md"):
            i += 1
            continue
        # The block: back to a blank line or a bullet start, forward to a blank or the next bullet.
        start = i
        while start > 0 and lines[start - 1].strip() and not re.match(r"^\s*- ", lines[start]):
            start -= 1

            end += 1

content.text:
I'd leave the order alone. Retitling is possible; reordering costs far more than it buys.

**What reordering would buy:** a tidier story. For example, `vc-dr-apply.sh`'s two rungs (5 and 8) side by side, and the three agent-files drafts together. That's real, but it's only how the history reads.

**What it costs:**
1. **A conflict at every rung.** Each rung bumps `Cargo.toml`'s version on the same line and edits the same ladder and record lines in `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`. Any reorder conflicts at every rung it moves. To keep the version suffixes in order, each rung's version and the ladder numbers would also have to be rewritten. It's the same churn as today's collapse, multiplied.
2. **The links to the agent side.** jj keeps change ids across a rebase, so the `ochid:` links survive. But the transcript is chronological, and a work history in a different order no longer matches it. `lookup` falls back on time when there's no trailer, and the open Todo **lookup is tested on a reordered ladder** exists precisely because this is unproven. We'd be the first test, on real history.
3. **Rungs 0 to 5 are published.** They're on `origin`'s topic bookmark, and the agent commit on `main` names them. Moving them means a force-push of the topic (your approval), plus `trailers --update` for every `pcid:` whose parent changed.
4. **Honesty.** The order is how it happened. Rung 8 exists because `wt6` hit a problem during rung 7's review, and the subsections tell that story in that order.

If the goal is grouping for a reader, the record can do that with no rewriting: the closing's Solution or the subsections can group "test repos", "`vc-dr-apply.sh`", "agent-files drafts" and "the record and `zTOC.md`".

**On titles:** changing them is cheaper, because a re-description keeps the change id. Two catches:
- **Rungs 7 to 9:** local, so changing them is easy. We just did.
- **The opening:** published. Retitling it is a bend of "the bookend pair keep their names". It needs a force-push and `trailers --update`, and I'm not sure we have a tool that re-describes a published commit and keeps its trailers. `commit -r` covers drafts, `squash --title` covers `@-` only, and **desc takes a title, body, and trailers** is a Todo, not yet built. I'd check that before promising it.

What I'd do: keep the order, and retitle only if the cycle's title would otherwise mislead. Closing under **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing**, with a Solution that says plainly what was done and what moved to the next cycle, may be honest enough. If you'd rather the title fit, I'd find a safe way to retitle the opening first.

content.text:
Agreed on all three. Here's how I'd do each.

**1. Retitling: there are two layers.**
- **The record's title is free to change.** The rules already allow a mid-cycle rename: it reaches the block's text and the unpublished rungs, and the published bookends keep their names. So I'd rename the cycle in the block to say what it did. For example, **feat: test repos, vc-dr-apply, and the v0.3.1-2 agent-files**, or your wording.
- **The bookend commits are the catch.** The opening is published as **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing opening**, and the closing's title is read from it. Two choices:
  - **(a) Keep the published pair** and close under the old commit title, with the renamed record. `git log --grep` finds the cycle by either name, which the rule anticipates. No force-push.
  - **(b) Rewrite the opening's description,** keeping its change id, then `trailers --update` and force-push the topic with your approval. I need to check that some `vc-x1` command can re-describe a published commit and keep its trailers. `commit -r` is for drafts, and **desc takes a title, body, and trailers** isn't built. I'd try it with `--dry-run` first.
  - (b) has a real payoff: the next cycle can take the original title, **feat: close, land, and push compose with testing**, which is what its rungs actually do, without two cycles sharing one name in `git log`.

**2. Keeping the remaining rungs in place.** Today the closing's move takes everything in `## In Progress`, from its first `###` to the section's end, so it would carry the unstarted rungs into `## Closed` too. Two ways to keep them:
- **The closing's own edit splits the block.** Rungs 10 to 18 and the original Problem and Deliberation become the next cycle's block, under its own `###` heading below this one's, a "staged" next cycle. The tool would then move only the first `###` block. That's a small change, and it bends "`## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles", since a staged block now sits there between Land and the next opening.
  - The next opening then needs no move. It bumps, writes the ladder into `zTOC.md`, and commits.
  - It's also a step toward **Parallel cycles**, where `## In Progress` holds more than one block.
- **The `zTOC.md` ladder:** the closing keeps this cycle's finished ladder for the landmark (rungs 0 to 9 plus the closing), and the next opening writes the staged cycle's ladder.

**3. How I'd split the remaining rungs:**
- **Small and standalone:** **feat: a test repo converts an existing repo**. It's useful for converting real repos, and `wt6`-style testing benefits right away.
- **The original subject**, close, land and push composing with testing:
  - the readers taking any mix of `ochid:` and `ocid:`
  - `ocid:` being real only when the agent commit came first
  - the `--closing` fix
  - `land` defaulting to `@-` and the work scope
  - the release-bookmark seal
  - testing leaving the cycle able to continue
  - commands saying where the cycle stands
  - the docs

  It could split further, into a "linking" cycle (the first two and the seal) and a "composing" cycle (the rest). That decision can wait until it opens.

Two decisions for you:
- Retitle with (a), the record only, or (b), also rewriting the published opening, if a safe re-describe exists?
- Stage the next cycle's block in `## In Progress` (a tool change plus the bend)? Or keep it simple: the closing moves everything, and the next opening restores the remaining rungs from the landmark's `## Closed`?

## In Progress
#### Solution

Provisional. Three steps, each doing one thing, that compose with testing:

- Every step leaves a state that can be tested, nothing half-done.
- A step may repeat, so the user can test, tweak, and close again.
- Testing does not disturb the cycle or block the next step.
- Each tester's binary says what it is, its suffix the build and its version the commit.
- Exit codes can be trusted, so the steps and the tests chain in a plain shell, and `vc-x1` does not
  run the tests itself.

The steps:
#### Acceptance check

By `vc-x1-dev`, on repos made by `init --test-repo <path>/<repo-name>`, in a table-driven test:

- An N:1 cycle: close leaves every `ocid:` at `xxxx`. A tweak and a second close work. `land` with no
  `--scope` leaves the agent repo alone, and a push to any other bookmark keeps `xxxx`, at any scope.

  leaves every rung's `xxxx` and SHA unchanged and the closing's tree identical, and pushes the agent
  repo first. Pushed to a second release bookmark, the commits are already sealed and nothing changes.
- A push to a release bookmark of work alone, with an agent commit no commit carries the SHA of, is an
  error naming `-s b` and `--yes`, and with `--yes` it publishes and warns. An unsealed closing naming
  another agent `@` is refused, and a release bookmark that moved is refused before anything is
  committed.
- The release bookmarks: with no key, `main` and `master`, so an old config works, and with `[release]
  bookmarks`, that list alone, a project's `main` then being an ordinary bookmark.
- A test between any two steps, `validate` or a suffixed build, changes nothing the next step depends
  on, and the next step runs.
- Two clones of one local remote give a moved trunk and another's commits, with no network.
- 1:1 pairs carry a real `ocid:` on every commit and never `xxxx`.
- `validate-desc` and `lookup` accept 1:1, N:1, 1:M, N:M, and mixed, and this repo's `main`, where every
  rung of **feat: improve trailers** carries an `ocid:`, reports what it reports today.
- close, land, and push each end by printing where the cycle stands and what may come next.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Deliberation
